stats.name: Trust
stats.notes: How much they rely on you.

places.name: Driftwood Café
places.notes: Six tables, one view, a toaster with opinions.

places.name: Beach
places.notes: Upturned boats, gulls, the best sunsets on the coast.

places.name: Your flat
places.notes: Above the bait shop. Smells like it.

items.name: Old letter
items.notes: Sealed, addressed to Mia. Found behind a loose board in the flat.

flags.notes: Set by the game while it rains. The talks only read it.

characters.name: You
characters.notes: The new barista. What they say is mostly the options they pick.

characters.name: Mia
characters.notes: Owns the Driftwood. Dry, quick, kinder than she lets on. Fixes the toaster daily.

relations.label: old friend, still owes her a window

characters.name: Leo
characters.notes: Fisherman and the oldest regular. Yellow raincoat, long stories, short patience.

characters.name: The Gull
characters.notes: No name, no fear, no manners. Turns up in other people's talks to steal food.

dialogues.title: First day at the Driftwood
dialogues.notes: The opening talk. Shows the ropes and hands over the first drinks.

lines.text: The bell over the door jingles. The café smells of coffee, salt and slightly burnt toast.
We open at eight. It's... oh. You're the new barista.
Sorry. I'm Mia. I own the place, which mostly means I fix the toaster.

options.text: What do I need to know?

reply.text: Espresso machine on the left. It hisses. Ignore the hissing.
If it screams, run.
Fishermen at dawn, tourists at noon, and Leo at all hours.
He'll want a lemonade. Cold enough to hurt his teeth.

options.text: Do I get a name tag?

lines.text: Of course. Hold still.
She writes on a sticker with great care and slaps it on your apron. It says: {player}.
Suits you.
Two espressos to practise on, and a lemonade for Leo. He'll show up. He always does.
Don't ask me to taste the lemonade. I can't stand the stuff.

effects.name: show_tutorial
effects.text: Show how the till and the espresso machine work.

dialogues.title: Leo's usual
dialogues.notes: Leo drops in every day for a very cold lemonade. Getting it right earns the invitation to the sunset.

reply.text: A man in a yellow raincoat drops onto the stool by the window. He smells of the sea. Mostly fish.
You're new. I'm Leo. Whatever Mia told you about me, none of it is true.
Morning, kid. You know what I want.

lines.text: My usual. {item}, cold enough to make my teeth hurt.

reply.text: Ahh. That's the stuff. You'll do, kid.
Espresso? I'll be awake until Thursday.
Fine. Thursday it is.
Nothing? Just the view, then. Fair enough.
{item}? Keep it, kid. My pockets are full of strange things already.
Bring me a lemonade next time and I'll tell you a secret.

lines.text: Here's a secret: the beach, any weekend evening. Best sunset on the coast. Free, too.
Don't tell the tourists.

dialogues.title: Closing time
dialogues.notes: Every evening: Mia pays up and sends the player home. How warm she is depends on trust and romance.

lines.text: {name} flips the sign on the door to CLOSED and counts the till twice.

reply.text: Not bad today. You only scared one tourist.
The mop's in the back. It misses you.

lines.text: Stay for one more coffee? On the house. Don't tell the owner.
Oh, wait. I'm the owner.

reply.text: One coffee turns into two. Outside, the waves keep time.
I'll hold you to that.

lines.text: Here's your pay. Don't spend it all on lemonade.

effects.name: close_shop
effects.text: Lights off, shutters down, the radio fades out.

dialogues.title: Rain on the windows
dialogues.notes: The game turns the rain flag on. Nobody comes in, and Mia sulks until something cheers her up.

lines.text: Rain drums on the windows. Not a single customer all morning.
Nobody wants coffee by the sea when the sea is falling on their heads.
Go on. Cheer me up. I dare you.

reply.text: A rose? For me?
Nobody's given me flowers in years. Don't tell Leo, he'll sulk.
An espresso. Two days here and you already know me.
Lemonade. On a day like this. Are you cheering me up or finishing me off?
Nothing? Well. You're standing here. That's something, I suppose.
{item}? Huh. Thanks. I think.

lines.text: You know what? Nobody's coming in this weather. Take the rest of the day off.

reply.text: Go, before I change my mind.

options.text: I'll stay and keep you company.

reply.text: The two of you watch the rain for a while. It's nicer than it sounds.

dialogues.title: Sunset on the beach
dialogues.notes: Only after Leo's invitation, on a dry weekend evening.

lines.text: The sun sinks into the sea like a coin into a slot. Leo is sitting on an upturned boat.
You came. Sit. The boat doesn't bite. The crabs under it might.

options.text: How long have you known Mia?
I'm just here for the sunset.

lines.text: A story. Let me see...

reply.text: Once I caught a tuna so big it towed me halfway to Portugal.
Lovely people. Terrible at giving tuna back.
Forty years at sea and I've never seen a mermaid.
Saw a merman once. He owed me money.
Skraa.
A gull lands on the boat, takes Leo's sandwich and leaves without a word of thanks.
That's the story. That's every story, really.
Mia? Forever. I'd jump in the sea for her. I'd complain the whole way down, mind.
We grew up on the same street. She stole my bait, I stole her apples.
Talking about her makes me miss her. Daft. She's two streets away.
Long enough to know better than to talk about her behind her back.

lines.text: The sky goes orange, then pink, then the colour of a bruise.
Here. Washed up this morning, still fresh. Somebody's date went badly.
Give it to someone who'll like it. Not me. I'd only put it in a bucket.

reply.text: He walks you to your door, explaining knots the whole way. All of them.
Suit yourself. Watch out for the gull.

dialogues.title: The old letter
dialogues.notes: Draft. Needs a second pass, and a talk with Leo after it: does he ever find out she read it?

reply.text: Mia is sitting at the end of the pier, shoes off, feet over the black water.
The café is dark but for one lamp. Mia is doing the accounts, and losing.

lines.text: Can't sleep either? Sit down.

options.text: I found this in my flat.

reply.text: At this hour? You're either a poet or a burglar.

lines.text: She turns the envelope over. Her name is on it, in faded ink.
That's Leo's handwriting. Your flat used to be his, you know.
She opens it, reads it twice, and laughs until she has to wipe her eyes.
“Dear Mia, I'm no good with words, so here are a few: your coffee is awful and I love you.”
Thirty years in a wall. The coward. The sweet, daft coward.

effects.name: play_music
effects.text: Something slow, then something less slow.
